I’m a proud son of a World War II veteran, my father, Clarence Burgess Owens. 

Born 100 years ago, my dad was raised during the era of the Great Depression and nationwide segregation. He and his two older brothers proudly volunteered to serve during WWII. 

My dad, due to his rifle skills, was part of our country’s first integrated reconnaissance team.

I was blessed to have had a Dad who was always my hero. He was exceptional but not “an exception” for the men of his generation. He knew how to dream big, work hard, compete for respect and, when necessary, run toward his fears, as did millions of young American soldiers during past wars. 

Last year I ran across notes in his journal that summarized his feelings, as a 20-year-old, upon returning home from the Philippines and Japan.

“I have fulfilled my dream to serve my country.”

This is what defines our history as a nation: brave, patriotic Americans who answer the call, serve our nation in uniform, and then, once that chapter is over, continue to find ways to serve our country.

To every veteran across this nation, to those who stormed beaches, patrolled jungles and deserts, and stood watch on quiet nights far from home, and to the families who waited and prayed for them: THANK YOU. 

Thank you for your courage. 

Thank you for your sacrifice. 

Thank you for saying “Send Me” when America needed you.

What an honor to be part of Salem, Utah’s American Preparatory Academy’s stirring Veterans Day program, where over 50 local Veterans were honored. 

Veterans Day is a sacred and special acknowledgment as we take time to reflect and honor our true American heroes. https://t.co/dBgg0RFtXg

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
